nothing reliable. Think about a cars brakes...when you hit them, pads squeeze the rotors... you are turning the kinetic energy the car has built up and transforming it into thermal energy. An aircraft uses the same type of thing when it applies air brakes..the drag creates friction. Step it up and look at a capsule entering the earths atmosphere, again, the air moving much faster than an airplane creates enough friction to transform the capsules velocity into heat. Does anyone else hate stupid articles like this? All they confirmed is that they think it might work. That's not what confirm means!!

In fact, they haven't even confirmed that; all they've confirmed is that it doesn't NOT work. There are still variables that could be influencing the results (which they stated), or it could actually be working. The only things they know for sure are:

  • There is definitely thrust being produced.
  • That thrust is definitely coming from the EM Drive, or it isn't.

So I understand why the EM drive could change propulsion forever, but what advantages does this offer for space travel exactly? I feel like the sheer amount of power required for an EM drive to propel anything into space would not be beneficial over a standard combustion rocket.
Chemical rockets are still the best at getting to space. Nothing else has the thrust density to overcome Earth's gravity.
Well, in theory some nuclear rocket designs could do it - and of course there's always Orion...

Energy can be collected indefinitely in space in the form of solar power.

Propellant mass cannot. With a traditional rocket you will eventually run out of fuel. More fuel = more mass = more expensive to launch.

Essentially. Massless reaction means you can achieve ridiculously energy efficient acceleration and deceleration. Hook an EM Drive up to, say, a nuclear reactor and you can get to Mars in a matter of weeks, rather than months. Jupiter in a few months, Pluto in a little over a year and a half.

Speeds that have, for all intents and purposes, been in the realm of science fiction become achievable. Hell, depending on the size of the reactor you could use an EM Drive to get to Proxima Centauri in a few hundred years, rather than the tens of thousands it'd take today. Probably less.

The benefit is you don't have to carry propellent.

Conventional rockets have to have mass that they eject to propel the rocket forward.

This drive needs no propellent. Which means that if you can generate electricity, you can, supposedly, move under thrust. So instead of 90% of the vehicle being occupied with propellent, you can carry other stuff, like, say, people.

Not only carrying people, but limitless "fuel." The issue with space travel is that the delta-v requires constant burning of fuel. Once you stop burning, the delta-v stops.

Right now, we thrust from Earth and do minimal thrusts to stay on track, but mostly "coast" through space. This is extremely slow and time-consuming.

An electronic engine that doesn't consume mass can be recharged via solar power and be left on almost indefinitely, constantly accelerating the craft towards the target. This should, in theory, speed up space travel exponentially.

Think about it like driving your car: you can get to your destination by giving it ONLY enough throttle to propel it over the uphill parts, and coast down the rest, or you can give it constant throttle the entire time... The latter obviously being the quickest.

This thing uses a ridiculous amount of power - 35MW per Newton of thrust, if I'm calculating it right.
